content_record.title: 75 minutes of weekly interval walking cut central fat in 315 adults
content_record.editorial_body: A small dose of interval walking could offer big benefits for adults with excess waist fat, a new trial suggests. 315 adults with central obesity walked briskly in intervals for 75 minutes weekly. One weekly session reduced body fat and waist size similarly to three sessions. Cardiovascular fitness improved equally in both groups after four months. Interval walking induces repeated cycles of high-intensity muscle contraction that increase AMPK activation and GLUT4 translocation, enhancing skeletal muscle glucose uptake and fat oxidation. The high-intensity bouts also stimulate catecholamine release, which promotes lipolysis in visceral adipose tissue via beta-adrenergic receptors, while the post-exercise oxygen consumption (EPOC) elevates 24-hour energy expenditure. These mechanisms explain how even a modest weekly dose of 75 minutes can reduce central fat, as the intermittent nature of the exercise triggers a more potent metabolic response per minute than continuous moderate exercise, consistent with Åstrand's interval training principles and Vague's emphasis on central fat as a metabolically active depot. This signal is based on This once-a-week workout may help cut belly fat, study shows from ScienceDaily Top Health. Read the original report for full context.
